primary_source.title: Efficient Online Conformal Selection with Limited Feedback

claim_checks.claim: Unprojected ACI preserves an exact telescoping validity identity, whereas projection can hide accumulated validity debt.
claim_checks.evidence: Theorem 1 uses the exact unprojected update lambda_{t+1}=lambda_t+eta(phi-Y_t) to telescope success deviations. Section 2.3.1 shows a projected update adds residual epsilon_t; if projection happens on a constant fraction of an interval, the normalized residual can be Theta(1). Lemma 1 gives a concrete three-arm adversarial outage where the projected rule has D_I=phi L and capped rounds have epsilon_t=-eta phi.
claim_checks.scope: This establishes failure of the natural projected variant in the paper and that projection invalidates the exact ACI accounting argument in general. It does not prove that every conceivable projected or clipped controller fails on every sequence.

claim_checks.claim: The pathwise target-tracking rate is O(1/sqrt(T)).
claim_checks.evidence: Theorem 1 gives interval error <=(Lambda+2 eta)/(eta L). With eta=1/sqrt(T), this is <=(Lambda sqrt(T)+2)/L. For the full horizon L=T and constant Lambda, average error is O(1/sqrt(T)) and cumulative deviation is O(sqrt(T)); for arbitrary shorter intervals the rate depends explicitly on L, and only L=omega(sqrt(T)) guarantees o(1) average error.
claim_checks.scope: Do not report a uniform O(1/sqrt(T)) guarantee for all intervals. The constant-Lambda interpretation uses the paper's bounded-parameter regime, including phi bounded away from 1 and, for the efficiency theorem, Lambda=C_max/(1-phi).

claim_checks.claim: The finite-arm stochastic efficiency regret is O(sqrt(n T log(nT))).
claim_checks.evidence: Theorem 2 with eta=1/sqrt(T) gives expected cost regret O((C_max/(1-phi))*sqrt(n T log(nT))) against the optimal stochastic policy satisfying expected validity. The stochastic result assumes i.i.d. reward/cost vectors and n=o(T).
claim_checks.scope: The pathwise/adversarial guarantee is the validity dimension; the efficiency-regret dimension is stochastic and must not be described as adversarial regret.

claim_checks.claim: Specific score/interval instantiations have weaker model-dependent rates near T^(2/3) and T^(3/4).
claim_checks.evidence: Corollary 1 discretizes scalar thresholds with delta=T^(-1/3) under monotonicity and Lipschitz expected cost to obtain tilde-O(T^(2/3)) expected efficiency regret. Corollary 2 discretizes intervals with delta=T^(-1/4) to obtain tilde-O(T^(3/4)).
claim_checks.scope: These are separate instantiations with their own assumptions and should not be collapsed into the finite-arm rate. Appendix A also contains a lighter success-only scalar controller with a different tradeoff.

claim_checks.claim: Boundary actions are merely an implementation preference.
claim_checks.evidence: The main model explicitly assumes a guaranteed-success arm with cost C_max/reward 1 and a guaranteed-failure arm with cost 0/reward 0. Step 2 chooses these arms when lambda crosses the upper/lower boundaries. Their deterministic drifts establish lambda in [-eta,Lambda+eta], which Theorem 1 uses directly. Theorem 2 separately uses p=1 on high-boundary steps and p=0,c=0 when lambda<=0 to control boundary time and regret.
claim_checks.scope: These exact boundary arms are structural assumptions of this algorithm/proof, not optional implementation details. The paper does not prove boundary actions are the unique possible way to stabilize an unprojected validity controller; a different mechanism preserving exact accounting would require a new proof.

empirical_scope.projected_vs_boundary_synthetic: Three-arm adversarial shift, phi=0.5, Lambda=2, eta=0.05, T=2000; supports the specific mechanism failure diagnostic.
empirical_scope.projected_vs_boundary_cifar100: Top-k arms {0,5,10,20,50,100}, phi=0.8 with adversarial ordering by true-label rank; projected baseline exhibits long local validity failure while boundary-stabilized ACI recovers.
empirical_scope.warning: These experiments illustrate the theorem mechanism; they are not a universal empirical benchmark for autonomous-research admission.

transfer_guard.supported: An autonomous admission controller may preserve an explicit cumulative validity/safety debt instead of silently clipping it, and can use an actual conservative action to pay down debt.
unsupported_without_new_evidence: sublinear efficiency regret under adversarial/non-i.i.d. costs
validity if no real guaranteed-success/guaranteed-failure actions exist
equivalence of arbitrary risk ledgers to conformal success indicators

material_correction_to_worker: The worker's mechanism is substantively supported, but the O(1/sqrt(T)) target-tracking statement must be tied to full-horizon (or sufficiently long interval) tracking and constant Lambda; the exact theorem is interval-dependent. Boundary actions are proof-critical structural assumptions for the presented main algorithm, not merely implementation choices. Projection is shown to break the exact identity and can fail linearly on a concrete adversarial instance, but this should not be generalized to every possible projected controller on every sequence.
unresolved: No theorem here gives an anytime target-only utility/no-negative-transfer fallback for autonomous research admission.
Transfer to settings without exact guaranteed-success and guaranteed-failure actions requires a new stabilizer and proof.
The stochastic efficiency benchmark remains i.i.d.; behavior under nonstationary efficiency costs is not covered by Theorem 2.
